Subject: model v4.2 p95 latency spike — timeouts in production

Hi Mina / Ben —

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency spike from model-v4.2 on our critical inference route (batching disabled) at ~09:45 PDT. Errors are timeouts (500) on ~2% of requests and p95 has moved from ~220ms to ~1.8s. We rolled a config change on our side (reduced concurrency) but the service is still failing several user flows.

Attached is a small snapshot of our SLO dashboard for the last 2 hours (p95_spike_slo_graph.png). We need to understand whether this is a model regression or something infra-related. If this is model-related, we want to request an immediate revert to v4.1 in our Dedicated pool — we are willing to accept a brief maintenance window to restore user experience.

Questions:
- Can Redwood confirm whether v4.2 shows kernel or KV-cache errors from the serving runtime?
- Do you support an emergency revert (automated rollback) for dedicated accounts, and what approvals are required?

This is impacting a payment flow so we'd like to proceed quickly.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Park
Head of Platform — Atlas Analytics

Subject: Re: model v4.2 p95 latency spike — timeouts in production

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the heads-up and the graph. We're investigating immediately. Ben and I will pull logs from the v4.2 serving pool and check for kernel fallback, OOMs, and KV cache thrash.

Short plan / asks:
- Ben: will start a live trace and check model hot-path (I flagged this as priority).
- Marissa: can you authorize an emergency revert gate for Atlas' Dedicated pool if we confirm a model regression? We prefer to run a single canary rollback to v4.1 and hold for 30 minutes for your team to validate, then a full revert if green.
- Chloe / Atlas SRE: please confirm the time window you prefer (we can do a rollout during the next 30–45 minutes if you approve).

We will attach any debug traces we collect. If a rollback happens, we'll document the SLA exception and any credit/impact afterwards.

Mina / Ben / Chloe —

I authorize a controlled emergency revert to model-v4.1 for Atlas' Dedicated pool under the following constraints:
- Run a canary at 10% traffic for 15 minutes, collect p95 + error-rate, and vendor logs.
- If canary shows p95 <= 300ms and error-rate < 0.5%, proceed to full revert with a rolling window (30 minutes).
- Create a ticket in our incident tracker (INC-ATL-759) and tag it as SLA-EXCEPTION.
- Notify Customer Success to offer a one-week SLO grace window and discuss any billing adjustments after postmortem.

Ben: please attach the debug trace when you reply (we'll need it for postmortem). Ben has retained elevated permissions for Dedicated reverts today.

I'll be on standby to approve the rollout; please do not perform a forceful rollback without the canary validation.

Following Marissa's approval we ran the approved canary at 10% traffic starting 14:10 PDT. Canary completed at 14:25 with p95 back to ~280ms and error-rate reduced to 0.3%. We proceeded with the rolling revert and the pool is now on model-v4.1.

Actions completed:
- Canary verification: p95 280ms, error-rate 0.3%
- Full rolling revert across Dedicated pool (completed 15:05 PDT)
- INC-ATL-759 opened and linked to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-48291
- Attached debug trace from the v4.2 hot path for follow-up (debug-trace.zip).

Next steps for Atlas: please validate your end-to-end flows and reply here when green. We'll leave the revert in place until you confirm stability (Marissa authorized a 30 minute hold after revert). After closure we'll run a short postmortem and discuss any SLO credits as part of the SLA exception.

Thanks for the quick coordination — sorry for the disruption.
